lead: A file is a named block of bytes on storage. Android gives your app two file homes. Internal storage is private, small, and always present. External storage is shared, larger, and may be removed. openFileOutput and openFileInput read and write files inside the app's files/ folder; getFilesDir() and getCacheDir() return the File objects for files/ and cache/. Apps use files for logs, downloaded images, exports, and caches. Only a few universities teach the mode flags and scoped-storage rules at this depth.
prereq: You need: Context and the package name from Unit 2, and the private key-value idea from Chapter 4.1.

sections.h3: Internal storage: private and always present

blocks.text: Internal storage lives under /data/data/<pkg>/ on the device. This area is private to the app. getFilesDir() returns files/. getCacheDir() returns cache/, which Android may clear when space is low. getDir(name, mode) creates or opens a named subfolder.

For simple files call openFileOutput(name, mode); it returns a FileOutputStream. openFileInput(name) returns a FileInputStream. MODE_PRIVATE keeps the file readable only by your app and is the safe default. MODE_APPEND adds to the end instead of replacing. MODE_WORLD_READABLE and MODE_WORLD_WRITABLE are deprecated; do not use them in new code.

Internal files need no permission and are always available, even when no SD card is present. They are deleted on uninstall, and the cache can be cleared earlier. A file the user must see in a file manager is a poor fit. Do long writes off the main thread; a slow write blocks the UI.

sections.h3: Writing and reading a text file

blocks.text: Open the file, wrap the byte stream in a character stream, write lines, close. try-with-resources closes the stream even if an exception occurs.

items: Pick the file name and mode: MODE_PRIVATE or MODE_APPEND.
Call openFileOutput(name, mode) to get a byte stream.
Wrap it in OutputStreamWriter and BufferedWriter to write text.
Write each line, then close the stream. Use try-with-resources.
To read, wrap openFileInput(name) in an InputStreamReader, then in a BufferedReader, and call readLine() until it returns null.

blocks.text: OutputStreamWriter uses the device default charset, which is UTF-8 on Android. Pass StandardCharsets.UTF_8 explicitly so the bytes are fixed and other tools can read the file. A small log fits in memory. A 5 MB log should stream in chunks, not build one giant String.

External storage may be a removable SD card or emulated shared storage. Before any write, compare Environment.getExternalStorageState() with Environment.MEDIA_MOUNTED. If it is not mounted, skip the write; the file will not appear.

getExternalFilesDir(type) returns your app's external folder, usually Android/data/<pkg>/files/. Pass null for the root or a type such as Environment.DIRECTORY_PICTURES. It returns null if external storage is not currently available; test for null before creating files in it. This folder is removed on uninstall and is the right place for a 5 MB log.

Shared public folders are different. Older apps asked for READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE and WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE. From Android 10 (API 29), scoped storage limits direct access to public folders. For shared media use MediaStore; for user-picked documents use the Storage Access Framework. Share files through a content provider, not a guessed path (Chapter 4.5).

figure.caption: Private files and cache sit under /data/data/<pkg>; the app's external folder is on removable storage that may be unmounted.

spec.aria: A storage tree splits into private internal storage holding files and cache, and external storage holding the app folder that may be unmounted.

examples.question: An app writes a 3-line log at 32 bytes per line and a 40 KB thumbnail. (a) Which folder for each? (b) Total bytes? (c) What happens on uninstall? (d) Where can a 5 MB log go, after what check?
steps: Log: 3 × 32 = 96 bytes; path getFilesDir()/log.txt because it is private and small.
Thumbnail: 40 × 1024 = 40,960 bytes; path getCacheDir() because it can be regenerated.
Total: 96 + 40,960 = 41,056 bytes. Both paths are under /data/data/<pkg>/; uninstall deletes both, and cache may be cleared earlier.
examples.answer: The log goes to getFilesDir(), the thumbnail to getCacheDir(), total 41,056 bytes; both are deleted on uninstall; a 5 MB log can use getExternalFilesDir(null) after the MEDIA_MOUNTED check.
examples.check:
lines = 3
per_line = 32
log_bytes = lines * per_line
thumb_kb = 40
thumb_bytes = thumb_kb * 1024
total_bytes = log_bytes + thumb_bytes
print(log_bytes)
print(thumb_bytes)
print(total_bytes)

traps: Writing external storage without checking state. When storage is not mounted, getExternalFilesDir() returns null, so building a File or stream from it throws NullPointerException, and a path on unmounted storage fails with FileNotFoundException. Check Environment.getExternalStorageState() equals MEDIA_MOUNTED and check the returned folder for null before writing.
Saying internal files survive uninstall. Both filesDir and cacheDir are deleted; cache may be cleared sooner.
Using MODE_WORLD_READABLE in new code. It is deprecated; share with a content provider.
Doing a 5 MB write on the main thread. The UI freezes; use a background thread and close streams with try-with-resources.

quiz.q: Which method returns the private files folder?
Why is getCacheDir() suitable for a thumbnail?
quiz.a: Android may delete it; the thumbnail can be regenerated.

quiz.q: An app writes 4 lines of 50 bytes and a 20 KB image. Total bytes?
An external write never appears. Give two causes and one fix.
quiz.a: Cause 1: storage not mounted. Cause 2: writing to a shared public path without READ/WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE on API 28 or lower, or using a guessed path under scoped storage. Fix: check MEDIA_MOUNTED (and null from getExternalFilesDir), and use the app-specific folder or MediaStore/SAF so permissions are correct.
Adds new bytes to the end of an existing file instead of replacing it.

quiz.q: Which folder for a 5 MB log, and what check comes first?

quiz.a: It is deprecated; it exposes the file to other apps. Share through a content provider instead.

beyond: Not for the exam. Modern Android routes shared media through MediaStore and SAF, and scoped storage removed broad file paths. Cloud sync and encrypted local caches are common in production. Search 'Android scoped storage', 'MediaStore', and 'Storage Access Framework' next.
